items.title: Enhanced quantum parameter estimation based on the Hardy paradox
items.abstractRawHtml: Statistical paradoxes such as the Hardy paradox and the enhancement of phase estimation via postselection both draw upon the same nonclassical features of quantum statistics described by nonpositive quasiprobabilities. In this paper, we introduce a postselected quantum metrology scenario where the initial state, the dynamics associated with the phase shift, and the postselection are all inspired by the Hardy paradox. Specifically, we identify an anomalous weak value that is characteristic of both the Hardy paradox and the potential enhancement of sensitivity by the postselection. We find that the efficiency of the enhancement is reduced when the expectation value associated with the anomalous weak value is different from the inverse of this value. We conclude that the relation between enhanced phase estimation and the Hardy paradox requires a detailed understanding of the relation between weak values and expectation values.

items.title: Linear-optical generation of hybrid Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill entanglement from small-amplitude cat states
items.abstractRawHtml: Hybrid bosonic codes combining bosonic codes with photon states offer a promising pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, the efficient generation of such states in optical setups remains technically challenging due to the requirement for complex non-Gaussian resources. In this paper, we propose a scheme to efficiently generate hybrid entangled states between a Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubit and a photon-number state using small-amplitude cat states as the primary resource. items.title: Partial reversibility and counterdiabatic driving in nearly integrable systems
items.abstractRawHtml: Adiabatic (or reversible) processes are the key concept unifying our understanding of thermodynamics and dynamical systems. Reversibility in the thermodynamic sense is understood as entropy-preserving processes, such as in the idealized Carnot engine, whereas in integrable dynamical systems, it is understood as the conservation of the action variables. Between these two idealized limits, however, things are much less clear. In this work, we study several toy models to assess the extent to which reversible processes are even possible in this regime. We then explore how the dissipative losses resulting from rapidly driving these kinds of systems can be fought by approximate counterdiabatic driving. Finally, we provide numerical evidence that much of the phenomenology should be the same for quantum many-body systems with large degeneracy in the presence of integrability breaking perturbations.

items.title: Directional quantum walks of two bosons on the Hatano-Nelson lattice
items.abstractRawHtml: We theoretically investigate the interplay of interactions and non-Hermiticity in the dynamics of two bosons on the one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson lattice with nonreciprocal tunneling. Next, we analyze the dynamics of this system in the presence of a static external force, F and demonstrate that non-Hermiticity leads to asymmetric two-particle Bloch oscillations. Interestingly, when F=0 (F≠0), strong interactions lead to the formation of an inner density-cone (density-hourglass) structure; this inner structure also becomes asymmetric in the presence of non-Hermiticity. We further analyze the spatial correlations that develop between the two bosons, and establish that the system exhibits nonreciprocal bunching (antibunching) in the presence of weak (strong) interactions. Finally, we examine the growth of the quantum Fisher information FQ with time, and demonstrate that FQ decreases with increasing δ. Interestingly however, for both one- and two-particle walks, the rapid growth of FQ characteristic of the Hermitian case, with an effective power law FQ∝tα, α≃3, persists in the presence of nonreciprocal tunneling.

items.title: Single- and two-parameter sensing near critical points in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model
items.abstractRawHtml: We investigate single- and two-parameter metrological responses near second-order critical boundaries and triple points in the anisotropic quantum Rabi model. To achieve two-parameter identifiability, we employ a coherent initial state in the parameter encoding. Near a second-order critical boundary, the residual quadratic dynamics enhances sensitivity but generally also introduces measurement incompatibility. In the triple-point limit, dynamical quadrature mixing is suppressed, while the coherent displacement preserves two independent parameter responses. Thus, the two coupling parameters remain locally identifiable while the mean symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) commutator tends to zero. We further derive an exact compatibility curve inside the normal phase. Along this locus, the two coupling parameters remain locally identifiable, and the Holevo and SLD Cramér-Rao bounds coincide. items.title: Multipartite Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality from interwoven frustrated down-conversion
items.abstractRawHtml: We present a theory of an interference process that starts with N coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion (PDC) sources, whose output modes are directed to N observers such that each observer receives modes from two different source crystals. By varying the local phases of the input modes, perfect 2N-photon interference is observed in 2N single-photon registrations, one in each output mode of the local PDCs. The interference results from the indistinguishability of the origins of the detected photons: either they all originate from the source PDCs or from the local PDCs. Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality of the process emerges when one considers situations in which at least one of the local PDC processes is blocked and the 2N-photon interference disappears. A “lifted” Clauser-Horne inequality is violated when its sole negative correlation term is tuned to maximal destructive interference, while all other terms involve settings in which one of the local pumps is off.

items.title: Light-induced line narrowing of the magnetic resonance in a parametric resonance optically pumped rubidium magnetometer
items.abstractRawHtml: Optically pumped atomic magnetometers are fundamentally limited by spin-exchange relaxation in finite magnetic fields. items.title: Charging efficiency bursts in a quantum battery with cyclic indefinite causal order
items.abstractRawHtml: Enhancement of quantum battery performance is a popular subject in quantum thermodynamics. An interesting phenomenon is the quick charging effect [Phys. Rev. The results validate the existence of charging efficiency bursts as shown by our theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

items.title: Topological defect states via local symmetry breaking in modified Haldane models
items.abstractRawHtml: Antichiral edge states extend the conventional bulk-edge correspondence by allowing edge modes on two parallel boundaries to propagate in the same direction, compensated by counterpropagating bulk states. However, their strong localization at physical boundaries leads to a severe dependence on boundary conditions and a lack of effective radiation suppression, hindering their practical application in optical communications. Here we propose a control mechanism based on local symmetry breaking in a modified Haldane photonic crystal. By tuning the geometric parameters of boundary rods, antichiral edge states can be merged into and hybridized with the projected bulk continuum. By reversing this mechanism, we create internal line defects that induce coupled interface modes inside the crystal. These modes form topological defect states that retain the unidirectional transport and topological origin of the antichiral system, while exhibiting quality factors several orders of magnitude higher than those of edge states. We experimentally demonstrate a defect waveguide and defect cavity and observe selective coupling from traveling waves to discrete circulating resonant modes. The resonant frequency can be tuned by geometric modulation. This work provides a low-loss and internally integrated route for constructing nonreciprocal topological photonic devices.

items.title: Simultaneous ground-state cooling of six mechanical modes of two levitated nanoparticles
items.abstractRawHtml: Ground-state cooling is a prerequisite for exploring macroscopic quantum effects in mechanical motion of massive objects. We also find that by properly tuning the polarization angle θ between the cavity field and the optical tweezer fields, the coupling channels can be controlled on demand and simultaneous ground-state cooling of these six motional modes of the two nanoparticles can be realized. items.title: Regular and chaotic dynamics of nonlinear optomechanical systems controlled by modulated light

items.title: Space-efficient quantum solvers for Boolean satisfiability problems via structural reduction
items.abstractRawHtml: The Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problem is a central benchmark for quantum optimization, but conventional encodings typically require one qubit per active variable, limiting their use on near-term quantum hardware. Here we introduce a space-efficient framework for one-in-three SAT based on the decisive chain reduction algorithm (DCRA), which exploits clause-induced dependences. For an instance generated with n variables and m clauses, let ñ be the number of active variables appearing in the clauses. The DCRA identifies s initial variables and expresses the remaining ñ−s active variables as linear combinations of them, reducing the effective search space from 2ñ to 2s. For positive random instances near the critical regime, we empirically find s close to ñ−m, yielding substantial qubit savings. In the reduced space, we derive a compact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization formulation whose problem Hamiltonian provides a common input for quantum annealing (QA), the quantum adiabatic algorithm (QAA), and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA). Numerical simulations validate the framework on instances with up to 150 variables for QA-based solvers and up to 50 variables for QAA- and QAOA-based implementations. For QA-based solvers, finite-size scaling on satisfiable positive random instances with up to 200 variables shows an approximately exponential decay of the mean success probability and reveals a clause-density-dependent tradeoff between qubit reduction and annealing hardness. On a superconducting processor, the six-qubit QAOA solves a 25-variable instance with ñ=21 active variables, achieving 12.62% success above the 4.69% uniform-sampling baseline. For a 13-variable instance, the DCRA achieves a measured success probability of 3.37%, compared to 0.05% with the direct encoding at equal shot budgets. These results demonstrate that structure-exploiting reductions offer a practical route to qubit-efficient quantum formulations of satisfiability problems on near-term hardware.

items.title: Direct large-area observation of subsurface plastic activity in conditioned copper electrodes
items.abstractRawHtml: High-field conditioning is the process by which radio-frequency structures in particle accelerators and other high-gradient devices reach their operating fields, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains an open question. The misorientation separates into three tiers (high-field center and edge, low-field periphery, and unexposed reference) that match the spatial profile of the conditioning-state variable ES predicted by Monte Carlo simulations. items.abstractRawHtml: Storage ring-based steady-state microbunching (SSMB) is a promising approach for generating high-average-power coherent radiation, while the instabilities driven by coherent undulator radiation in the laser modulator (LM) are important for the ring performance. The evolution of the wakefield in the longitudinal beam dynamics equations is derived, and the instability growth rates are analyzed. Numerical simulations show excellent agreement with the theoretical model, validating the mode-decomposition approach. These findings provide critical insights into the design and operation of SSMB storage rings, suggesting effective mitigation strategies to suppress the instability and enhance the overall performance.

items.title: Emittance preservation under multifaceted CSR effects in isochronous deflection structures for multikiloampere bunches
items.abstractRawHtml: In modern accelerator facilities, coherent synchrotron radiation (CSR) presents a fundamental limitation to maintaining high-brightness electron-beam quality during deflection, with accurate modeling of its effects remaining an outstanding challenge. This study introduces a novel optimization method using an integral approach to suppress CSR-induced transverse emittance degradation under two representative bunch scenarios: ultrashort bunches and high-charge long bunches. We present analytical solutions for suppressing CSR effects in the dipoles across several quadruple-bend-achromat (QBA) layouts and establish general conditions for mitigating CSR-induced emittance growth in the subsequent drift sections of isochronous beamlines. Our analysis demonstrates that the QBA is the minimal configuration capable of simultaneously suppressing transverse emittance degradation and preserving the longitudinal beam distribution. Beam tracking results show negligible emittance growth for multikiloampere bunches at a 16° deflection. Furthermore, multicell simulation confirms the exact scalability of this approach. While previous designs suffer severe emittance degradation upon cascading, the QBA maintains exceptionally preserved beam quality.

items.title: Engineered metal-insulator transition in rare-earth nickelate thin films for near-room-temperature zero-differential thermal emission
items.abstractRawHtml: Materials with thermally tunable optical properties offer a powerful route to modulate infrared radiative signatures without active cooling or heating. Among them, compounds exhibiting a metal-insulator transition (MIT) are particularly attractive, as they enable abrupt and reversible changes in infrared emissivity near technologically relevant temperatures. Here, we investigate epitaxial Sm1–x Ndx NiO3 (0.15<x<0.4) thin films as a tunable material platform for near-room-temperature infrared emissivity control. By engineering epitaxial strain and composition, we achieve precise control over both the MIT temperature and its sharpness near ambient conditions, enabling broadband long-wavelength infrared (LWIR) emissivity modulation. The resulting emissivity reduction follows an effective T^{-4} dependence, compensating the intrinsic T^4 scaling of blackbody radiation and yielding nearly constant LWIR radiated power over a temperature span of approximately 15 C. Moreover, outdoor thermal imaging directly confirms the zero-differential thermal emitter (ZDTE) behavior through a quasi-constant apparent temperature. These findings establish rare-earth nickelate epitaxial films as a versatile platform for passive and adaptive infrared emission control near room temperature, with expected impact in thermal management and infrared signature control.

items.title: Distinct low-frequency noise fingerprints of filamentary and interfacial switching in La 2 NiO 4 + δ -based RRAM
items.abstractRawHtml: This work investigates the noise characteristics of filamentary- and interfacial-type resistive random-access memory devices in a single material system based on La2NiO4+δ, using low-frequency noise spectroscopy across different resistance states, read voltages, and device sizes. We observe a clear difference in the noise properties of the two device types: (i) filamentary devices exhibit overall elevated noise levels compared with the interfacial ones, (ii) the relative noise magnitude between high (HRS) and low resistance states (LRS) in the two device types is inverted: elevated noise is present in the HRS of filamentary devices and in the LRS of interfacial ones and vice versa, (iii) no area dependence of noise properties is observed for the filamentary devices, whereas interfacial devices show a size-dependent frequency exponent and noise magnitude scaling. For both switching mechanisms, a systematic two-stage noise suppression with increasing read voltages is observed, which is found to be correlated with the transition from ohmic to space-charge-limited conduction. Our study links noise characteristics to the underlying switching and conduction mechanisms of oxygen vacancy migration-based memories.

items.title: Generation of attosecond electron bunches via high-gradient acceleration in periodic structures driven by a pulse-front-tilted laser
items.abstractRawHtml: Direct laser acceleration leveraging transverse fields promises unparalleled gradients exceeding 1  TeV/m yet is fundamentally constrained by phase slippage, which limits interaction length and final energy gain. Here, we overcome this dephasing limitation by employing a pulse-front-tilted laser interacting with a plasma grating. This configuration ensures sustained phase matching, facilitating extended acceleration and stable near-field confinement. Uniquely, this structure functions as a phase-selective sieve that generates dense electron bunches with durations of hundreds of attoseconds. Particle-in-cell simulations demonstrate that a 61 J laser pulse yields an 11 pC beam with energies surpassing 10 GeV at gradients of approximately 2  TeV/m. Derived for an idealized dephasingless regime, linear scaling laws predict that 1 kJ pulses can drive beams to 200 GeV. These findings present a promising pathway toward on-chip TeV-scale accelerators and attosecond sources, with potential applications for high-energy colliders, ultrafast electron imaging, and advanced light sources.

items.title: Taiji drag-free and attitude control system: Modeling and end-to-end simulation for the science mode
items.abstractRawHtml: In the Taiji project—a Chinese space-borne gravitational wave detector—the drag-free and attitude control system (DFACS) is the core technology responsible for maintaining the inertial motion of the test mass (TM). A thorough understanding of the spacecraft (SC) dynamic behavior under complex gravitational perturbations and multisource nongravitational disturbances is crucial for optimizing control system design, studying data processing pipelines, and verifying the detector performance. In this paper, we propose a unified simulation framework integrating the constellation orbital motion with a full-state closed-loop DFACS system and develop a 60-degrees-of-freedom (DoF) DFACS simulator. Furthermore, benefiting from the introduction of high-precision numerical methods, the simulator is extended to 31 significant digits, which supports high-fidelity numerical simulations of the intersatellite laser interferometry measurements from picometers to million kilometers. Three different experiments are implemented to assess the performance of DFACS by analyzing the single TM’s residual force noise, moving optical subassembly’s jitter, and the arm-length variation of TM-TM and SC-SC. Moreover, we quantitatively demonstrate the feasibility of decoupling DFACS design and orbit optimization. For the Taiji project, this study enables a more realistic on-orbit simulation of the detector and provides a representative system response under closed-loop control, supporting more accurate detector sensitivity analysis and facilitating refined optimization for scientific objectives.

items.title: Inhomogeneity of magnetic anisotropy and damping in nanoscale magnetic tunnel junctions
items.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the Gilbert damping constant α and the inhomogeneity of the effective magnetic anisotropy field HKeff in nanoscale magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with various free-layer diameters D, which have two different structures possessing different magnetic properties around the pattern edge. Homodyne-detected ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) is used, allowing to disentangle the inhomogeneous broadening ΔH0 owing to the spatial variation of HKeff from the effects of damping in the linewidth of spectra. We find that ΔH0 increases with decrease in D, while α is almost constant. The degree of the increase in ΔH0 is found to change with the MTJ structure. We show that these results are explained by a model considering the distribution of a demagnetizing field that increases with the decrease in D. The obtained findings provide important insights for the development of nanoscale MTJs with high reliability and high efficiency.

items.title: Dimensional confinement-driven scattering inversion in NaCrTe 2
items.abstractRawHtml: Dimensionality reduction provides a powerful route to tune the electronic and magnetic properties of van der Waals materials, yet its influence on electronic transport remains complex due to competing effects from quantum confinement and modified scattering mechanisms. Here, we investigate this interplay in an antiferromagnetic semiconductor NaCrTe2 using first-principles calculations combined with the Boltzmann transport equation beyond the constant relaxation time approximation. Our results show that the monolayer limit induces a coupled magnetostructural reconstruction, reducing the band gap from 0.44 eV (bulk) to 0.15 eV (monolayer) and significantly enhancing the static dielectric constant. This evolution triggers a fundamental scattering inversion: whereas bulk transport is limited by polar optical phonon scattering, the monolayer becomes dominated by acoustic deformation potential scattering. We show that this crossover originates from the simultaneous suppression of the Fröhlich interaction through enhanced dielectric screening and the amplification of acoustic scattering due to pronounced lattice softening. These results clarify how the interplay between dielectric screening, lattice stiffness, and band topology governs transport in low-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, providing a framework to optimize their electronic performance.

items.title: Zn 2 + and Mn 2 + doping effect on spin dynamics of Fe 3 O 4 -based magnetic nanoparticles: A possible path to efficient MRI contrast agents
items.abstractRawHtml: Iron oxide-based magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) play a major role as contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The introduction of Zn2+ and Mn2+ ions within their crystal lattice alters the magnetic anisotropy and the spin dynamical properties of the systems, which in turn influence the nuclear relaxation mechanisms that drive contrast enhancement in MRI. This work explored two sets of doped-magnetite MNPs (chemical formula ZnxMnyFe3−x−yO4) with core diameters of d∼4 or 15 nm produced by the fast and reproducible microwave-assisted synthesis method, and using different solvents like water or polyols. The d∼4  nm MNPs were doped with Zn2+, from x=0 to 0.9; for Zn2+=0.5, Mn2+ was introduced at y=0.2,0.4. The d∼15  nm MNPs were doped with Zn2+ from x=0 to 0.4, with Mn2+ added at y=0.1 for Zn2+=0.3 and at 0.3 for Zn2+=0.4. Both sets were dispersed in water with carboxymethyl-dextran or polyacrylic acid coatings to ensure their colloidal stability, even under high magnetic fields. We highlighted the influence of the size and of the Zn2+/Mn2+ doping on the static and dynamical magnetic properties, also through the H1-NMR-dispersion profile analysis over a wide frequency range and the application of the superparamagnetic relaxation heuristic model. Larger particles exhibited higher nuclear relaxometric efficiency and anisotropy compared to the smaller ones, consistently outperforming the commercial contrast agents. On the other hand, the magnetic response and the nuclear relaxivities are enhanced by a Zn2+ content of x=0.1 ions for approximately 4  nm MNPs and of x=0.4 for approximately 15  nm MNPs, while a slight enhancing effect was obtained by Mn2+ introduction. It is thus shown how a proper size and doping combination provide an attractive way to modify the static and dynamical magnetic properties of MNPs by acting on different spin-spin correlation times dominating in specific frequency intervals, thus enabling the fine-tuning of image contrast properties suitable for magnetic resonance imaging.

items.title: Simultaneous determination of local magnetic fields and sensor orientation with nitrogen-vacancy centers in nanodiamond
items.abstractRawHtml: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in nanodiamonds have emerged as a promising quantum sensing platform for biomedical imaging applications, yet random orientations of individual particles present significant challenges in large-scale sensor calibration. In this study, we demonstrate a novel approach to simultaneously determine each particle’s crystallographic axes and the surrounding local vector magnetic field. Specifically, a minimum of four distinct bias fields is required to unambiguously extract both the orientation and the local field. We validate our method experimentally using NV centers in two scenarios: (i) in a bulk diamond with known crystal orientation as a proof of concept and (ii) on various single nanodiamonds to mimic real-world applications. Our work represents a crucial step toward unlocking the full potential of nanodiamonds for advanced applications such as in situ biomedical imaging and nanoscale sensing in complex environments.

items.title: Generation of perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices
items.abstractRawHtml: Spatiotemporal (ST) vortices carrying transverse orbital angular momentum have attracted growing interest in both optics and acoustics. However, despite diverse generation schemes, a fundamental limitation persists: the vortex radius increases with the topological charge, leading to a size mismatch that complicates efficient multiplexing and detection. Here, we introduce the concept of perfect ST acoustic vortices to decouple the vortex size from the topological charge. Unlike conventional counterparts, these vortices maintain a nearly constant radius regardless of the topological charge. We theoretically construct this new class of vortices via the Fourier transform of an ST Bessel-Gaussian spectrum in the wave-vector-frequency domain. Experimentally, we implement the synthesis using a one-dimensional acoustic phased array. We then characterize the generated fields, confirming their size invariance and investigating their propagation and superposition properties. By enabling a nearly charge-independent vortex radius, our work overcomes a critical constraint of ST acoustic vortices, paving the way for high-capacity acoustic communications, sensing, and particle manipulation.

items.title: Measurement-induced state transitions across the fluxonium qubit landscape
items.abstractRawHtml: Understanding the mechanisms that limit high-fidelity readout in circuit quantum electrodynamics is essential for its optimization. Multiphoton resonances are understood to be a limiting factor, causing population transfer from the computational states to higher-energy states under drive. This effect, known as measurement-induced state transitions, has been extensively studied for the transmon qubit. While this exploration has begun for the fluxonium qubit, a systematic study of this effect is lacking. Here, we bridge this gap by theoretically studying measurement-induced state transitions in the fluxonium qubit over a wide range of parameters, comprising essentially all experimentally explored ranges. We find that lighter fluxoniums are less susceptible to these state transitions when compared with their heavier counterparts. We attribute this effect to the combination of lower density of multiphoton resonances, a smaller requisite coupling for a given dispersive shift, and a more harmoniclike structure of the charge operator. We confirm the validity of our analysis by performing time-dependent readout simulations. Finally, we consider the impact of the superinductor’s array modes on measurement-induced state transitions over a large range of parameters.

items.title: Deterministically addressing spins at clock transitions with a frequency- and bandwidth-tunable superconducting resonator
items.abstractRawHtml: Solid-state spin ensembles addressed via superconducting circuits are promising candidates for quantum memory applications, offering multimodal storage capability and second-long coherence times at their clock transition. Implementing practical memory schemes requires dynamic control over both the resonator frequency and bandwidth, and most crucially, deterministic access to the clock transitions. In this article, we report measurements of a superconducting resonator whose frequency can be tuned by passing a DC current through the high-kinetic-inductance thin film, and whose bandwidth can be tuned by parametric coupling to a low-Q buffer resonator. Using this resonator, we deterministically address an ensemble of bismuth donors at their clock transition, measuring a Hahn-echo coherence time of 450 ms. We demonstrate RF driving of the bismuth donor hyperfine transitions, as well as dynamic bandwidth control of the resonator.

items.title: Muonium dynamics as a probe for depth-resolved properties of 4 H − SiC
items.abstractRawHtml: This study establishes a baseline for muonium (Mu) charge-exchange dynamics in n-type 4H−SiC through a detailed low-energy muon spin rotation (LE−μSR) investigation. Epitaxially grown and ion-implanted samples with nitrogen and phosphorus donors were characterized to assess the effect of carrier concentration and doping method on defect formation. LE−μSR enabled nanometer-scale depth profiling of near-surface and implanted regions, revealing variations in charge carrier concentration due to fixed surface charges. The temperature dependence of the diamagnetic fraction and phase provided direct evidence of the Mu0 to Mu− transition, with extracted activation energies consistent with known donor ionization energies. Additionally, high-field μSR was used to analyze the Mu dynamics, and Monte Carlo simulations were used to model the Mu0 electron capture process. The simulation results offer a quantitative method to extract free electron concentrations from LE−μSR data, enhancing its capability to characterize the activation of dopants and carrier depth profiles. We demonstrate that LE−μSR is a powerful depth-resolved tool that can provide insights for optimizing the fabrication of reliable SiC devices for power electronics.

items.title: Adiabatic self-vibrations generated by inelastic Andreev tunneling in a movable Cooper-pair box
items.abstractRawHtml: Self-sustained oscillators produce stable periodic motion robust to dissipation. Such motion is usually achieved by work fed back into the oscillator, but its performance is often limited by frequency-dependent operation. Here, we propose a scheme for self-sustained vibrations without external feedback. We consider a movable Cooper-pair box attached to the free end of a voltage-biased normal-metal pillar. The Cooper-pair box carries an Andreev current subject to an electric field applied perpendicular to the current. In the adiabatic limit, where the Cooper-pair box state follows its motion, vibrational instability occurs, pumped by inelastic Andreev tunneling. Nonlinearity of the Josephson coupling saturates the vibrational amplitude, resulting in two-dimensional self-vibrations. We discuss the advantage of this adiabatic scheme in comparison with feedback-induced self-oscillation.

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in p -doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstractRawHtml: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show, analytically and numerically, that in p-doped semiconductors such coupling can be strongly enhanced. Moreover, the relative coupling strength increases with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The theory is applied to Si resonators, where doping is often used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

items.title: Planar multiplexed elastic-wave bound states in the continuum in two-dimensional Lamb-wave phononic crystal plates
items.abstractRawHtml: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable elastic-wave resonances with ultralow radiation loss, but in multimode plates, localized modes readily couple to multiple radiation channels. Here we extend a symmetry-mismatch design recently implemented in one-dimensional Lamb-wave structures to a two-dimensional phononic crystal plate and realize elastic BICs and quasi-BICs by exploiting a mismatch between symmetric (S) and antisymmetric (A) Lamb modes. The plate is engineered such that the A mode forms a passband while the S mode exhibits a band gap; a central defect then hosts localized S modes whose eigenfrequencies lie in this band gap yet overlap the A-mode continuum, forming S-mode BICs. Finite-element simulations and laser Doppler vibrometry show that the number of BIC modes can be controlled by varying the number of defect unit cells. By weakly breaking the midplane mirror symmetry through tilted hole sidewalls, we induce controlled S−A hybridization and convert these strictly bound states into quasi-BICs that are efficiently excited by plane waves. Using this mechanism, we implement a planar multicavity structure where spatially separated quasi-BIC resonators are addressed at distinct frequencies, thereby realizing planar space-frequency multiplexing and providing a simple route to multifrequency elastic-wave signal processing and integrated phononic circuits.

items.title: Electronic structure, quasiparticle renormalizations, and magnetic correlations in the alternating single-layer bilayer nickelate La 5 Ni 3 O 11
items.abstractRawHtml: Using the DFT+dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) method we study the normal-state electronic structure, orbital-dependent quasiparticle renormalizations, Fermi surface, and magnetic correlations in the recently discovered alternating single-layer bilayer hybrid Raddlesden-Popper nickelate superconductor La5Ni3O11 (1212-LNO). Our results for the DFT+DMFT electronic states exhibit qualitative differences for the structurally distinct single-layer and bilayer Ni ions, implying the importance of confinement and orbital-dependent correlations. The partially occupied Ni eg electronic states originating from the bilayer Ni ions form strongly renormalized quasiparticle bands with a large enhancement factor m*/m∼3.5 and 4.2 for the Ni x2−y2 and 3z2−r2 orbitals, respectively, implying the proximity of the Ni 3d states to orbital-dependent localization. Moreover, the eg states of the single-layer Ni ions exhibit an orbital-selective Mott insulating state, with a narrow energy gap for the Ni 3z2−r2 states and metallic, strongly incoherent (non-Fermi-liquid) Ni x2−y2 ones. Our analysis of magnetic correlations suggests the formation of intertwined spin and charge density wave stripes in the bilayer NiO6 slab, in close similarity to the double-layer material. We refine two major instabilities, a leading one is associated with a propagating wave vector ${\bf Q}=(\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ ({associated, e.g., with anup-down-0" spin pattern ord8–d8–d8L_’’ charge-density wave with Ni d8L_ ions bonded in an interlayer spin polaron}), competing with the bicollinear (14,14) (``up-up-down-down") stripe state. In contrast, the single-layer Ni 3d electrons exhibit instability toward the N'eel-type magnetic state. Under pressure, 1212-LNO undergoes an orbital-selective Mott insulator-to-metal phase transition, associated with metallization of the single-layer Ni eg states. As a result, the single-layer Ni eg bands exhibit non-Fermi-liquid (bad metal) behavior with strongly incoherent spectral weights near the Fermi level. We note that correlation effects result in a remarkable reconstruction of the symmetry and strength of magnetic correlations as compared to that obtained within DFT. In fact, we observe a crossover from single-layer (as obtained within DFT) to double-layer dominated magnetic correlations.

items.title: Heterogeneous ferroelectricity and conductivity of oxidized BaTiO 3 crystals: Role of nanoscale phase segregation in the surface region
items.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the effect of thermal oxidation on BaTiO3 single crystals. Our results reveal that, even at moderate temperatures of up to 1000 °C, complex segregation mechanisms occur involving the movement of Ba-rich compounds to the upper surface, where they form inhomogeneously distributed BaO nanocrystals. As a result, deeper regions of the surface layer become depleted in Ba and become TiO2-rich. A sandwich-like structure evolves in the surface layer, exhibiting a measurable electromotive force and self-polarization. This, in turn, screens the polarization and diminishes the global ferroelectric response. The conductivity is also strongly influenced by the irreversible segregation effects in the surface region. An as-received crystal can be transformed into a metallic state, while oxidation induces semiconducting properties and prevents a return to the metallic state upon subsequent reduction. Nanoscale analysis demonstrates that the conductivity is channeled to filaments forming along dislocations, whose local chemical composition changes upon reduction and oxidation even at moderate temperatures due to preferential Ba and O pipe diffusion thus determining the electric behavior of the whole sample.

items.title: Anisotropic magnon spin transport in CrPS 4
items.abstractRawHtml: Crystal anisotropy provides a powerful route for realizing direction-dependent transport in solid-state systems. While its influence on electronic transport is well established, the role of anisotropy in magnon spin transport in van der Waals magnets is largely unexplored. Here, in a nonlocal geometry, utilizing the monoclinic van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS, we observe pronounced anisotropy in both electrically and in thermally excited magnon spin transport. Electrically generated magnons exhibit a magnon spin conductivity at least 2.2 times larger and a spin diffusion length at least 2.7 times longer for transport along the crystallographic- axis compared to the crystallographic- axis, where λma∼ 211 nm and λmb≥ 575 nm. In comparison, at 8T, we find the nonlocal second-harmonic resistance associated with thermally excited magnons to be $7timeslargeralongthecrystallographic−𝑏axisat25K.Wefurthershowthatamagnonspindiffusionlengthcannotbereliablyextractedfromthenonlocalsecond−harmonicresistance,owingtotheextendedtemperatureprofilewithinCrPS_4.Likewise,weshowthattheanisotropyinthespinSeebeckcoefficientscannotbereliablyestimatedfromthethermallyexcitedmagnonspintransportalone,asitisintertwinedwiththeanisotropicheatconductivityofCrPS_4$. Utilizing the electrically generated magnon spin transport, we demonstrate that intrinsic crystalline anisotropy serves as an effective control parameter for tuning magnon spin transport, opening new avenues for magnonic device engineering.

items.title: Low-temperature spin freezing and diffuse magnetic correlations in Tb 2 Zr 2 − x Ti x O 7 ( x =0, 0.5)
items.abstractRawHtml: We report the thermodynamic behavior and short-range magnetic correlations in the Tb2Zr2O7 and Tb2Zr1.5Ti0.5O7 compounds. The parent compound Tb2Zr2O7 has defect fluorite structure, which evolves toward the pyrochlore phase on Ti doping at the Zr site. There is no long-range magnetic order down to 0.4 K, and a magnetic field dependent spin freezing evolves below ~ 1.3 K and ~ 1.0 K for the parent and doped compounds respectively. The ac susceptibility measurements indicate slow spin relaxation processes below ~ 20 K in both compounds. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals broad diffuse scattering, indicative of short-range correlations at low temperature, owing to local structural distortions and persistent spin fluctuations. Our data show that changing the defect-fluorite to the pyrochlore structure through Zr-doping yields only moderate changes of the magnetism dynamics while the overall qualitative response remains unaffected.

items.title: Magnetization flip caused by magnetic field rotation in compensated Ni 4 Nb 2 O 9 ferrimagnet with exchange bias
items.abstractRawHtml: A single-crystal compensated ferrimagnet Ni4Nb2O9, consisting of two antiferromagnetically coupled ferromagnetic (FM) Ni2+ layers with opposite moments in the ab plane, exhibiting noninterface exchange bias (EB), was investigated. The magnetization hysteresis loops M(θ), measured at a weak field H rotating in FM layers clockwise and then counterclockwise, show two successive M flips in opposite directions with a large hysteresis of the flip angle θMR. It was found that the angle θMR shifts due to EB to higher or lower values, depending on the sign of the unidirectional anisotropy EB specified by the field cooling protocol. Furthermore, the EB effect also influences the temperature of spontaneous switching Tsw from negative to positive magnetization, which occurs below Tcomp=33K, at a constant field H. Namely, Tsw decreases in the presence of positive unidirectional anisotropy and increases in the presence of negative anisotropy, indicating that the energy required to flip M depends on the sign of EB. The features discovered allow us to more fully comprehend the nature of the EB effect in coupled FM layers of compensated Ni4Nb2O9 ferrimagnet.

items.title: Curvature-controlled spin-wave localization and soft-mode instabilities in magnetic nanotube multilayers
items.abstractRawHtml: We investigate collective spin-wave excitations and curvature-driven instabilities in concentrically arranged nanotubes coupled via antiferromagnetic interlayer exchange. By solving the linearized Landau–Lifshitz equation including exchange, anisotropy, interlayer exchange coupling, and nonlocal dipolar interactions, we show that curvature substantially reshapes the spin-wave spectrum and the spatial structure of the eigenmodes. As the number of nanotubes increases, the spectrum evolves into a multiband structure with hybridized collective branches and surface-localized modes. In contrast to planar multilayers, the tubular geometry breaks the equivalence between inner and outer boundaries, producing asymmetric surface localization, curvature-induced shifts of the nodal structure, and nonreciprocal spin-wave propagation. We further analyze magnetic instabilities through the softening of the lowest spin-wave modes. For weak radial anisotropy, a uniform mode governs the instability, whereas above a critical anisotropy the soft mode occurs at a finite wave vector, signaling an instability toward a stripelike modulation along the nanotube axis. Although curvature shifts the instability thresholds, the characteristic modulation period remains nearly independent of the tube radius. The overall dynamical behavior of the coupled nanotubes can be understood in terms of an effective curvature-induced anisotropy, which unifies the spectral reconstruction and instability thresholds. These results establish tubular multilayers as a platform in which geometry controls both collective spin-wave excitations and instability-driven magnetic phases.

items.title: Clock-transition-enabled long electron spin coherence of telecom emitters in CeO 2
items.abstractRawHtml: Rare-earth-ion-doped crystals have emerged as a promising platform for quantum technologies, owing to their narrow telecom-band optical emission, long spin memory, and compatibility with silicon integrated photonic architectures. However, the realization of scalable quantum devices requires host materials with intrinsically dilute spin environments to suppress decoherence. In this context, erbium (Er3+) doped cerium oxide (CeO2) is an attractive candidate due to the ultralow concentration of nuclear spins in the host matrix and its compatibility with silicon-based technologies. Here we perform a comprehensive investigation of the coherence properties of an Er3+ electron spin qubit in CeO2 via semiclassical as well as detailed cluster correlation expansion simulations. By systematically exploring magnetic field strength, pulse sequences, erbium concentration, and spin temperature, we identify regimes where decoherence from the spin bath is strongly suppressed. Our investigations illustrate that at dilute doping concentration (of the order of 10 ppb) and sub-Kelvin temperatures, operation near clock transitions enables Hahn-echo coherence times to approach the second timescale even at natural isotopic abundance. Importantly, from a practical standpoint, coherence times on the order of ∼10 ms are expected even at liquid helium temperature (about 2 K) for similar concentrations. Moreover, we demonstrate that an additional enhancement can be obtained with conventional multi-π-pulse dynamical decoupling protocols. Thus, our findings establish Er3+ doped CeO2 as a front-runner for realizing spin qubits, quantum memories, and integrated quantum networks.

items.title: Exploring entropic orders: High-temperature continuous symmetry breaking and topological order
items.abstractRawHtml: High temperature is usually expected to destroy order: as the Gibbs state approaches the infinite-temperature limit, it becomes an equal-weight ensemble over all states and the system is generically disordered. Recent works showed that entropic order can violate this expectation through coupling to bosons in classical lattice models and quantum field theories, where the ordered states have higher entropy. Here we present new analytic methods for constructing quantum lattice models that exhibit entropic orders. In particular, we construct quantum lattice models with continuous symmetry breaking at high temperature in 1+1 dimensions and clarify how entropic order can evade the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorems. We also construct high-temperature entropic p+ip chiral topological superconducting states in 2+1 dimensions with temperature-independent anyon correlation functions. In addition, we obtain a broad family of high-temperature entropic nonchiral topological orders. We show that the entropic topological orders have strong higher-form symmetries at high temperature unlike the conventional topological orders, and the symmetry is spontaneously broken. These results follow from two general constructions that couple a given lattice model with a low-temperature ordered phase either to ordered bosons, or for local commuting-projector Hamiltonians, to more general bosonic degrees of freedom.

items.title: Topological zero-reflection points in multiterminal quantum wire junctions
items.abstractRawHtml: We study scattering in noninteracting multiterminal quantum wire junctions and show that junctions with dihedral symmetry can exhibit exact zero-reflection points for N≥4 terminals. By analyzing the scattering matrix, we identify these reflectionless points in the (E,t′) parameter space, where E is the incident particle energy and t′ is the junction hopping amplitude. These points exhibit an even-odd dependence on N and converge asymptotically to a common limiting value in the large-N limit. We show that the reflectionless points are characterized by an integer winding number associated with the phase of the reflection amplitude, providing a topological description for their stability against weak on-site disorder. We also consider junctions with broken time-reversal symmetry and find that a magnetic flux can induce additional reflectionless points, including for the N=3 case. For a four-terminal junction threaded by a π-flux, we identify a unique parameter regime in which the reflection amplitude vanishes over the entire energy band. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures through the behavior of Friedel oscillations and examine the stability of these reflectionless points in the presence of weak interactions.

items.title: Nondiffusive phonon transport in complex diamond microstructures and nanostructures
items.abstractRawHtml: The ultrahigh thermal conductivity of diamond, relevant to the momentum-conserving phonon normal process, holds exceptional promise for advanced micro/nanoscale thermal management. However, efficient modeling of collective phonon transport in complex three-dimensional diamond structures remains challenging. Here, we develop a computational approach for phonon transport in complex diamond micro- and nanostructures by directly solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation under Callaway's dual relaxation model with first-principles inputs. As a result, our model provides a good quantitative explanation of the thermal conductivities of diamond nanowires, nanobeams and cuboids. Furthermore, we analyze the effects of size and temperature on mode-resolved phonon hydrodynamic transport in natural and isotopically purified diamond microfilms. Finally, the computational framework is applied to porous diamond structures to reveal the effects of neck width and isotopic concentration on nondiffusive phonon transport. This work thus promotes both efficient modeling and physical insights into collective phonon transport in diamond micro- and nanostructures, offering guidance for future experimental measurements and engineering applications.

items.title: Altermagnetic band geometry and the antiferromagnetic thermal boundary in a coupled fermion-Ising model
items.abstractRawHtml: We study a minimal square-lattice model to examine the relation between momentum-space altermagnetic band geometry and real-space Ising criticality in a coupled fermion-Ising setting. In this model, itinerant fermions with explicitly spin-dependent nearest-neighbor hopping are locally coupled to transverse-field Ising moments. The hopping anisotropy parameter α tunes a dx2−y2-type altermagnetic band geometry in momentum space, whereas the transverse field h controls real-space antiferromagnetic (AFM) fluctuations and drives the finite-temperature AFM–paramagnetic (PM) transition of the Ising sector. Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we show for the representative α<1 case studied in detail, α=0.5, that the momentum-space band-geometry fingerprint remains visible in the coupled system: the spin-resolved occupation imbalance n↑(k)−n↓(k) displays a sign-changing structure that follows the underlying spin-split Fermi-surface geometry. By contrast, finite-size scaling of the staggered Ising order parameter indicates that, in the representative comparison between α=0.5 and 1.0, the extracted thermal critical fields remain numerically close on the scale resolved by our finite-size analysis at both T/t=0.5 and 0.2. We argue that this separation reflects the coexistence of a tunable momentum-space altermagnetic band geometry with the nesting structure of the half-filled nearest-neighbor bare kinetic term, which remains an important constraint on the AFM channel in this benchmark. Our results show that, in this controlled setting, a visible altermagnetic band-geometry fingerprint in momentum space need not imply a comparably large shift of the collective real-space magnetic phase boundary.

items.title: Merging bound states in the continuum into an exceptional point via magnetic field
items.abstractRawHtml: Exceptional points (EPs) and bound states in the continuum (BICs) are two distinct types of optical singularities that have attracted significant attention for their potential. While EPs are known for their enhanced sensitivity to perturbations, their performance in passive resonator systems is often limited by radiation losses. Conversely, BICs are ideal nonradiating resonances with theoretically infinite Q factors. Here, we explore the interplay between these singularities under time-reversal T symmetry breaking. We demonstrate the realization of an EP by merging two symmetry-protected BICs corresponding to the E2 representation in a C6v-symmetric photonic crystal slab composed of magneto-optical material. By applying an external magnetic field, we introduce an additional mechanism to break T symmetry, which competes with the intrinsic radiation losses of the open system. Our simulations show that the two BICs coalesce at the Γ point, forming an EP. This work unveils the interaction between different forms of T symmetry breaking and provides a controllable pathway for dynamically inducing EPs from BICs with infinite Q factors, with potential implications for sensing and tunable photonic devices.

items.title: Three-dimensional flat band in the topological electride of t -KAl
items.abstractRawHtml: By means of first-principles calculations and crystal structure predictions, we identify a series of potassium-aluminum (K-Al) compounds under high pressure, which are absent in ambient conditions. Among them, the P4/nmm KAl phase, stable under pressure from 15 to 70 GPa, exhibits a range of intriguing electronic properties, including a three-dimensional (3D) flat band near Γ, a composite nodal network, and 3D interstitial anionic electrons (IAEs). The 3D flat band of the highest valence band leads to a Van Hove singularity (VHS) with two saddle points near Γ. In addition, there exists a visible band inversion between the K-d- and the Al-p-dominant bands, which generates a composite nodal network without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), and evolves into a Dirac semimetal once SOC is included. Furthermore, calculations of local charge distributions indicate the existence of IAEs. Notably, the IAE2c and IAE8i states make a significant contribution to the 3D flat band and composite nodal network. Thus, our study not only enriches the phase diagram of a K-Al system, but also proposes a potential platform for studying the interplay among a 3D flat band, a 3D flat-band-induced VHS, and a 3D topological electride behavior.

items.title: Defect-nucleated charge density wave in monolayer 1 H − NbSe 2
items.abstractRawHtml: Reduced dimensionality is generally expected to enhance charge density wave (CDW) order. However, experimental results in monolayer NbSe2 appear conflicting: while optical measurements reveal CDW signatures up to 145 K on oxide substrates, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) studies on graphene-supported monolayers reveal no evidence of CDW above the bulk transition temperature (33 K), suggesting the absence of a dimensionality-driven enhancement. This discrepancy raises fundamental questions about the nature of CDW in the monolayer limit and the role of substrate interactions. Here, we use STM to investigate monolayer NbSe2 on graphene and directly resolve local 3×3 CDW modulation persisting to 77 K, well above the bulk transition. Distinct from coherent long-range CDW orders, the observed CDW modulation is short-ranged, nucleates preferentially at atomic-scale defects, and exhibits defect-selective pinning analogous to bulk behavior. Compared to bulk NbSe2, the CDW correlation length is significantly enhanced but remains spatially inhomogeneous, varying across flakes with different twist angles relative to the graphene substrate. These results indicate that reduced dimensionality indeed promotes CDW correlation in monolayer NbSe2. However, the stronger dielectric screening provided by graphene, compared to insulating oxides, likely contributes to the suppression of phase-coherent, quasi-long-range CDW order. Overall, our findings highlight the roles of dimensionality and substrate in determining CDW behavior in the monolayer limit.

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstractRawHtml: Superconductor–semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe–Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong-coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and nonrobust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak-coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while nonrobust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Tunable and suppressible non-Hermitian skin effect induced by non-Abelian gauge fields
items.abstractRawHtml: We theoretically investigate a tunable and suppressible non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) in lattice systems governed by non-Abelian SU(2) gauge fields, Zeeman field, and spin-dependent gain and loss. We show that non-Abelian hopping alone can generate a parity-dependent discrepancy between open- and periodic-boundary spectra, even in the absence of the NHSE. A uniform Zeeman field or spin-dependent gain and loss activates a direction-selective NHSEs, whereas their coexistence gives rise to a bipolar NHSE. Strikingly, we find that a spatially nonuniform Zeeman field generically suppresses the NHSE and drives boundary-accumulated skin modes back into the bulk, irrespective of the modulation profile. This suppression originates from the competition between skin-induced boundary accumulation and gradient-induced Wannier–Stark-like localization. Our results reveal versatile and experimentally accessible mechanisms for engineering, tuning, and suppressing non-Hermitian boundary localization, and provide a promising route toward exploring non-Abelian non-Hermitian physics in platforms such as electrical circuits.

items.title: Néel-vector-orientation induced direction-robust spin filtering in two-dimensional altermagnets
items.abstractRawHtml: Whether an antiferromagnet can host direction-robust spin-polarized transport without a conventional spin-selective band gap remains a central challenge in antiferromagnetic spintronics. Here, we establish a gapless, direction-robust spin-filtering mechanism in a compensated two-dimensional altermagnetic Weyl semimetal that requires neither a spin-selective band gap nor a large velocity contrast between spin projections. Using Janus monolayer Ta2TeSeO as a realistic platform, we combine symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, full-Brillouin-zone Wannier interpolation, and semiclassical transport. Rotating the Néel vector removes a unitary-mirror constraint and shifts one Weyl-cone pair away from its parent high-symmetry line. For an in-plane Néel vector, the residual C2zT symmetry forbids the independent σy mass that would open a local gap, allowing the reconstructed cones to shift in momentum while remaining gapless. Breaking unitary C2z simultaneously lifts the energy equivalence of the remaining mirror-pinned Weyl cones. The resulting coexistence of a metallic spin-projected manifold and a low-density-of-states (DOS) Weyl-derived manifold produces a predominantly DOS-driven conductance imbalance. At charge neutrality and 20 K, the longitudinal conductivity polarization for n∥x remains positive for every in-plane current direction and ranges from 76.4% to 82.0%. The symmetry-related in-plane Néel orientations provide two distinct spin-filtering states. This Néel-vector-driven symmetry mechanism provides a general route to direction-robust gapless spin filtering in compensated altermagnets.

items.title: Coexistence of magnon-induced optical vortex and Gaussian beam scattering assisted by rotational umklapp process
items.abstractRawHtml: The exploitation of crystal-lattice symmetries to engineer angular momentum transfer between structured light and magnons marks a novel frontier for optomagnonic research. In Brillouin light scattering, when focused light propagates parallel to an external magnetic field and interacts with ferromagnetic uniform magnons, only optical vortex scattering is expected to be permitted. Due to the combined effects of magneto-optical coupling and optical spin-orbit interaction, the transfer of magnon spin angular momentum to photon orbital angular momentum allows for this distinctive scattering phenomenon. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that, for a specific ferromagnetic crystal orientation, Gaussian beam scattering coexists with the optical vortex scattering, contrary to conventional expectations based on angular momentum conservation between magnons and photons. We show that the crystal lattice, via the rotational umklapp process, provides the missing angular momentum required for the Gaussian beam scattering. Furthermore, our theoretical model predicts a focus-dependent efficiency crossover between Gaussian beam and optical vortex scattering as the numerical aperture increases.

items.title: First-principles prediction of infrared optical properties of insulators using a resonant photon-phonon interaction model
items.abstractRawHtml: We present a simplified formalism for predicting infrared optical constants from first-principles calculations by considering resonant interaction between infrared photons and the crystal lattice. Addressing limitations of the widely used four-parameter semiquantum Lorentz model, the proposed approach bridges the gap between the harmonic three-parameter model and the rigorous many-body Green's-function-based approaches. By incorporating essential anharmonic effects including four-phonon scattering and phonon renormalization, the model provides an efficient and accurate alternative while maintaining low computational cost. The frequency-dependent refractive indices of MgO and rutile TiO2 are computed and compared with experimental data, demonstrating good quantitative agreement. The framework offers a practical approach for predicting optical properties of materials across a wide range of materials.

items.title: Directional selection of field-induced phases by weak anisotropy in triangular-lattice K 2 Mn ( SeO 3 ) 2
items.abstractRawHtml: Triangular-lattice systems host a variety of ground states, ranging from quantum spin liquids to magnetically ordered phases, the latter of which can exhibit a sequence of magnetic phase transitions under applied magnetic fields. Here, we report magnetic and thermodynamic measurements, combined with powder and single-crystal neutron diffraction, on a high-spin, nearly isotropic Mn2+ triangular-lattice system K2Mn(SeO3)2. The compound undergoes long-range magnetic ordering below TN∼4K in zero field. Contrary to expectations for an ideal Heisenberg system, an up-down-zero (UD0) magnetic structure is favored down to the lowest temperature (0.05 K), rather than the commonly expected Y-type structure. This UD0 state is, however, highly sensitive to external magnetic fields. For fields applied along the c axis, it is readily destabilized and replaced by the Y-type structure, followed by an up-up-down (UUD) phase corresponding to the 1/3 magnetization plateau. In contrast, when the field is applied within the triangular plane, the system evolves into a canted Y state at a higher critical field. These results reveal that weak anisotropy, though small in magnitude, exerts a strongly orientation-dependent influence, playing a key role in selecting the field-induced phases in this frustrated magnet.

items.title: Tuning the Fermi surface of MoTe 2 by Nb doping
items.abstractRawHtml: Ab initio calculations and angle-resolved photoemission experiments demonstrate that the bulk and surface electronic structure of Weyl semimetal candidate MoTe2 changes significantly by tuning the chemical potential by less than 0.4 eV. Calculations indicate that several Lifshitz transitions can occur among multiple electron and hole Fermi pockets of differing orbital character. Experiments show that 18% Nb-Mo substitution reduces the occupation of bulk and (001) surface bands, effectively producing a quasirigid band shift of ≈0.2eV. Orbital character and dimensionality of the bulk bands is examined by soft-x-ray angle-resolved photoemission with control of the excitation light polarization. Deposition of alkali-metal atoms on the surface produces electron binding energy shifts consistent with increased band filling. The results indicate that multiple regimes of electronic properties can be easily accessed in this versatile, layered material.

items.title: Self-consistent thermalization of electrons and phonons in the Hubbard-Holstein model
items.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the dynamics of the Hubbard–Holstein model after a sudden switch-on of the electron–phonon interaction within nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). Using the self-consistent Migdal approximation for the electron–phonon coupling together with self-consistent second-order perturbation theory for the electron–electron interaction, we show that the relaxation dynamics exhibits a crossover between electron-dominated and phonon-dominated regimes, extending to finite Hubbard interaction the scenario previously identified in the Holstein model. To investigate the emergence of a self-consistent thermalization of the electron–phonon system, we analyze the DMFT dynamics by enforcing the self-consistency after each global time-evolution, rather than at every time step. This allows us to follow the build-up of a self-consistent thermal bath. In the plane of real time and DMFT iteration number, thermalization is marked by a sharp propagating front. This front appears in electronic observables already for weak quenches within the simulated time window, whereas the phononic sector exhibits a visible front only at sufficiently strong coupling. Thus, at weak coupling the local dispersionless phonons show a delayed onset of front formation, while near and beyond the crossover the front develops on comparable timescales in both the electronic and phononic sectors. Whenever both fronts are resolved, they propagate with the same velocity, showing that thermalization spreads coherently through the coupled electron–phonon system.

items.title: Thermoelectric enhancement from an asymmetric spectral-conductivity cusp in spin-1 chiral fermions
items.abstractRawHtml: A recent study showed that, in spin-1 chiral fermion systems composed of two linearly dispersing bands and one trivial band, impurity scattering produces an asymmetric cusp in the spectral conductivity σ(ε). We demonstrate that this asymmetric cusp markedly enhances the electronic thermoelectric response. Using linear-response theory within the self-consistent Born approximation, we find low-temperature enhancements in both the Seebeck coefficient and the electronic figure of merit. Increasing the curvature of the trivial band further strengthens this cusp-induced enhancement, even though the corresponding density of states becomes smoother. To clarify this mechanism, we introduce a minimal cusp model for σ(ε) and show that the enhancement is most pronounced when the cusp is sharp and strongly asymmetric and when the spectral conductivity at the cusp energy is small.

items.title: Qubit encodings in the silicon p -orbital-valley spectrum for enhanced coherence and tunable two-qubit interaction
items.abstractRawHtml: We consider possible encodings of a qubit within the space spanned by the p-orbital manifold of an anisotropic silicon quantum dot, including the effects of alloy disorder. We find two types of avoided crossing in this manifold: one due to alloy disorder and one due to an out-of-plane magnetic field. Defining a qubit at such an avoided crossing offers prolonged coherence time and complete single-qubit control using baseband electrical control of the dot anisotropy. Using a phenomenological two-level fluctuator dipole noise model, we estimate an average dephasing time of T2*≈10µs and a quality factor of Q∼104. At the avoided crossing due to magnetic field, the qubit is a minor adaptation of the previously proposed pO qubit, spanned by the ground and excited p orbitals in the ground valley. However, at the avoided crossing due to alloy disorder, the qubit is qualitatively different, spanning the ground p orbital in the excited valley and the excited p orbital in the ground valley, and we dub it the pOv qubit. While the charge noise robustness is similar for pO and pOv qubits, we find that pOv qubits have desirable interaction properties. Namely, in contrast to the always-on transverse Coulomb coupling of pO qubits, we show that transverse coupling between pOv qubits is negligible, leaving only a longitudinal two-qubit interaction that can be tuned by modulating the orientation of adjacent elliptical dots.

items.title: r -process nuclei in the rare-earth region above N = 126 in relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory: A preponderance of shape coexistence in nuclei
items.abstractRawHtml: The shell structure of nuclei beyond N=126 relevant to the third peak at A≈195 in r-process nuclear abundances in investigated. Within the framework of the relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in deformed space, a comparative study of the response of nuclei with three different model Lagrangians, NL-SV1, SVI-2, and NL3, is made. Ground-state properties of even-even nuclei in the isotopic chains of Z=58–72 in the highly neutron-rich region are investigated. A comparison of binding energies with mass formulas shows that in the extreme region of the r-process path, the RMF model SVI-2 without nonlinearities of σ and ω mesons shows an excellent agreement with the mass formula HFB-24. It is shown that in all the above Lagrangian models, in the neutron rich region between the shell closures N=126 and N=184, there is a preponderance of nuclides exhibiting coexistence of well-deformed prolate and oblate shapes in the ground state. A prolate ground state is shown to evolve smoothly to a coexisting oblate ground state via a near degeneracy with successive addition of neutrons. Induced by an onset of deformation for N≥130, nuclei approaching the r-process path are shown to exhibit enhanced stability in many isotopic chains (Z>60). This has the effect of shifting the expected neutron drip line significantly farther into the neutron-rich region especially for the higher Z chains. Consequences of the enhanced stability, the shape co-existence and degeneracy of shapes in nuclei on the r-process nucleosynthesis are discussed.

items.title: Coulomb and nuclear polarization of the nucleon density in the dinuclear configuration of the Ca 40 + Pb 208 system
items.abstractRawHtml: The change of the nucleon density distribution of a heavy nucleus caused by the presence of a second nucleus at a fixed center-to-center distance is studied in the framework of the deformed Woods–Saxon mean field. The single-particle problem of one nucleus has been solved by diagonalization in a cylindrical harmonic-oscillator basis with the external field of the partner nucleus included in the Hamiltonian before diagonalization. The external field consists of the Coulomb potential of the partner charge distribution and of the nuclear part obtained by double folding of the Migdal density-dependent effective nucleon-nucleon interaction, in the same form as used in the dinuclear system approach. The induced density change δρ(r;R) and the corresponding changes of the quadrupole moment, of the mean-square radius and of the interaction energy have been calculated for the Ca40+Pb208 system at separations R=15.5–20 fm. The results are compared with the first-order (linear-response) treatment of the same external field. Because the mean field is anchored at the origin, the multipole moments are shown to require a translationally invariant definition: a displaced but undeformed distribution acquires a quadrupole moment second order in the displacement, and in this problem that kinematic term is comparable with the induced moment itself. Once it is removed, the intrinsic quadrupole response of Pb208 agrees with the first-order one to better than half a percent, and remains so over the full range of the switching parameter for the Coulomb field at R=20 fm, while that of Ca40 retains a genuine higher-order contribution of 12% to 16%. The polarization of both partners is dominated by the repulsive Coulomb tidal field, which produces an oblate deformation of the density, while the attractive nuclear field acts in the opposite sense and partially cancels the Coulomb contribution at the smallest separations. At the larger separations the induced octupole deformation is close to 40% of the quadrupole one for Pb208 and to 50% for Ca40, and it is the more sensitive indicator of the breakdown of the one-center picture. The polarization energy is a dipole quantity, the induced quadrupole deformation contributing only a few percent of it; it is verified by coupling-constant integration and is quoted under several correction prescriptions for the spurious translational component and for the absence of the residual interaction. The sensitivity to the geometry of the folding densities and the limits of validity of the one-center description are established quantitatively.

items.title: Physics-guided residual correction of α -decay half-lives based on the effective liquid drop model
items.abstractRawHtml: To improve the prediction accuracy of α-decay half-lives in heavy and superheavy nuclei, a physics-guided residual-correction framework combining the effective liquid drop model (ELDM) with machine-learning methods is proposed. The ELDM is first used as the macroscopic baseline for describing the barrier-penetration process, and XGBoost and TabPFN models are then employed to learn the residual deviations between ELDM predictions and experimental data. Several physically motivated descriptors associated with nuclear deformation, Coulomb-decay-energy systematics, and minimum orbital angular momentum are introduced into the residual-learning process. In the global 10-fold cross-validation comparison, TabPFN-term3 achieves the lowest prediction errors, reducing the root-mean-square error and mean absolute error from 0.567 and 0.417 for the ELDM baseline to 0.348 and 0.248, corresponding to improvements of 38.62% and 40.53%, respectively. Regional, parity-separated, and superheavy extrapolation analyses further support the effectiveness and transferability of the residual-correction framework. Overall, the proposed approach effectively reduces systematic deviations not fully described by the macroscopic ELDM baseline while retaining a direct connection to the underlying α-decay physics.

items.title: Investigation of transfer coupling strength in the N 14 + Hf 178 reaction
items.abstractRawHtml: Disentangling the effects of nucleon transfer via Q value and deformation on fusion has been a longstanding objective. To address this, a comparative analysis of the barrier distribution, which is an alternative probe to fusion, for the N14+Hf178 and O16+Hf178 systems have been performed. The consistent alteration in deformation by choosing the same target Hf178 mitigates its influence, thereby allowing for an explicit investigation of the effect of the Q value of nucleon transfer for these above systems. Consequently, the quasielastic scattering was measured for N14+Hf178 at backward angles. The extracted excitation function and barrier distribution were analyzed in light of coupled-channel calculations, which indicated a significant contribution from the one- and two-neutron transfer channels, alongside the rotational degrees of freedom in the highly deformed Hf178 nucleus. Furthermore, the coupling strength was extracted using the chi-square minimization method, yielding a value ≈0.201. The extracted coupling strength of N14+Hf178 system was compared with that of the two-neutron transfer in the O16+Hf178 system, which indicates that the coupling strength for nucleon transfer decreases with an increase in the Q value. This observed behavior might be due to the spectroscopic structures of the O16 and N14. The present study indicates that the spectroscopic properties play a significant role, along with Q values, in influencing the fusion reaction dynamics.

items.title: Probing neutron skin through event-by-event pion asymmetry in heavy-ion collisions
items.abstractRawHtml: In this work, we propose a novel approach for probing the neutron skin thickness of gold (Au) by analyzing the event-by-event distribution of π− and π+ yield differences. This is achieved through SMASH simulations of ultraperipheral Au+Au collisions at sNN=3GeV. Our results demonstrate that the mean value of Δnπ=nπ−−nπ+, along with the Pearson correlation and mutual information between (π−+π+) and (π−−π+), all scale linearly with the neutron skin thickness. Moreover, the slope of the line connecting two distinct Δnπ values in the event-by-event distribution also exhibits a linear dependence on the neutron skin thickness. The most sensitive Δnπ pairs are identified as (−2,−1), (−1,1), (0,1), and (0,2). These findings establish a new pathway for determining the neutron skin thickness. Finally, by comparing SMASH, JAM, and ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics simulations under identical initial conditions, we observed a certain degree of model dependence in the outcomes, yet the overall trends remained consistent. However, by extracting slopes from multiple Δnπ pairs in experimental event-by-event data and inferring the corresponding neutron skin thickness, one can assess which model better aligns with the true physical value.

items.title: Pion valence structure at intermediate x in the residual-field approach
items.abstractRawHtml: We calculate the valence parton distribution function (PDF) of pion within the theoretical approach based on spectral function representation of valence quarks in the pion. In this approach we assume that the soft partonic structure of pion is defined by the valence qq¯ cluster, consisting of current quarks, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The valence PDF is calculated using phenomenological light-front wave functions for the qq¯ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF (xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the valence quark cluster and the mass of the residual system. Magnitudes of these parameters are obtained by fitting to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF evaluated at starting Q0. They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed to describe existing pion PDFs at intermediate x. They also indicate that the qq¯ cluster is highly virtual and on average the interacting quark carries almost all of the momentum of the qq¯ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF and practically describing ≈(1−x) behavior observed recently at x→1 limit. Our nontrivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at x→1 limit.
